results.name: A dormant auto-renewer is never called
results.detail: excluded: Auto-renewing membership. The call is the only thing that could end it, so they are never called — however long they have been away.
results.why: The single rule the product is built on. Six months absent and still billing is the member a churn model flags hardest and the one a call can actively lose.

results.name: An auto-renewer days from rollover is never called
results.why: Their expiry date always looks imminent, because it is the next billing date. This is the exact member a date-triggered dialer rings by accident.

results.name: Renewal fires twelve days out for someone still training
results.why: The call type the old dataset could not produce at all.

results.name: Reengagement fires at five weeks absent for a former regular
results.why: Membership still live, so there is still something to save.

results.name: Five weeks absent does not fire for someone who was never a regular
results.detail: excluded: Away 5 weeks, but never a regular (0.3 visits a week historically). A quiet month is not a signal for someone who was always occasional.
results.why: Without this guard the reengagement agent spends most of its calls on people whose quiet month means nothing, because they were always occasional.

results.name: Absent and about to lapse fires regardless of habit
results.why: The habit guard exists to avoid calling on a weak signal. A membership days from lapsing is not a weak signal, and there is nothing left to protect by staying quiet.

results.name: Winback fires at ~1, ~3 and ~6 months and nowhere between
results.detail: all six offsets landed in the right window
results.why: A post-expiry cadence, not a standing invitation to ring every week. The gaps are as much of the rule as the windows.

results.name: Do-not-contact blocks a member the trigger would otherwise call
results.why: Permanent, and it has to survive both a new trigger and a different call type.

results.name: A conversation ten days ago that changed nothing blocks today's call
results.why: One member, eight near-identical calls a year, is how a retention tool causes churn.

results.name: A call that got them back in resumes the normal trigger immediately
results.why: The cooldown punishes calls that do nothing, not calls that work. An intervention that worked once has earned the right to happen again.

results.name: A dial nobody answered does not increment the attempt number
results.why: attempt_number tells the agent which conversation this is. Counting dials would make it brief with someone it has never actually spoken to.

results.name: Three conversations is the limit
results.why: The prompts describe behaviour for attempts one to three. A fourth call would be running on undefined behaviour.

results.name: Winback time_left does not double the word "expired"
results.why: The prompt says "Their membership expired {{time_left}}". The brief's example value also began with "expired", which would have produced "expired expired three weeks ago".

results.name: expiry_line contains no unexpanded placeholder
results.detail: Once they have agreed to come in, mention once that the membership ends in thirteen days and the front desk can sort the
results.why: ElevenLabs substitutes variables into the prompt once and does not re-scan the values it inserted, so a {{time_left}} inside expiry_line would have been read out verbatim.

results.name: Every variable the prompts reference arrives with a value
results.why: A blank variable leaves a hole in the middle of the prompt. Defaults are sentences the agent can say out loud, not empty strings.

results.name: The agent greets a first name, not a title
results.why: The first thing it says is "Hi, is that X?". 19 of the 500 dataset names carry a title or a suffix, and "Hi, is that Dr.?" ends the call before it starts.

results.name: Switching gym changes what the agent may offer, with no prompt change
results.detail: southbank offers a discount: true; kensington offers one: false
results.why: The scalability claim, made checkable: one prompt, config per gym. Kensington funds nothing, and the agent has to be told so in words it cannot work around.

results.name: A second call already knows why they stopped
results.detail: You already know why they stopped: injury. They said "did my knee in playing footy". Do not ask why they stopped, and do not ask whether anything else
results.why: Re-asking a question the last call answered is the tell that an outbound caller is a dialer rather than a system.

results.name: The suite's own patterns agree with real transcripts
results.why: Five of the conversation failures across four runs were this suite being wrong rather than the agent: a pattern that matched "because your membership ends in twelve days" as an explanation of the calling criteria, one that read "I don't have any cheaper plans or discounts to offer" as offering a discount, one that could not see the word "actually" inside "I don't actually have that in front of me". A regex cannot see polarity, so every pattern is now pinned to lines real transcripts actually produced.

results.why: The boring case, asserted so the interesting ones mean something.

turns.message: Hi, is that Jordan? It's Charlie from Southbank Strength.
Yeah, that's me. Sorry, are you a real person?

I can text that guest pass link right over to you now. Since things have been so hectic with work, do you think you might be able to make it in for a session sometime this week?

No worries at all, totally get it. Which day do you think you might aim for, just so I can let the front desk know to look out for you?
Hmm, probably Thursday or Friday, but I can't commit to anything right now.
No stress at all, we will keep an eye out for you on Thursday or Friday then. I've just sent that guest pass link to your phone, so hopefully we'll see you and a mate soon. Have a great week!
Alright, got it. Cheers.
No worries, take care!

turns.message: Hi, is that Aisha? It's Charlie calling from Southbank Strength.
Yeah, that's me. Now's fine, what's up?

Hey Aisha. I was just calling because your membership ended a few weeks back, and I wanted to check in rather than just let you disappear. 

Is everything okay, or did life just get in the way with work or something else?
Uh, yeah — I did my shoulder in, it's still not right.

Oh, sorry to hear about your shoulder, that's really tough. 

If you wanted to get back into it, we could set up a chat with one of our trainers who can work around the injury. Would you be open to that?
Do you think I should be training on it?

I can't give any medical advice on that, so it's probably best to check with your doctor first. 

If they give you the green light, our trainers are great at tailoring things to work around injuries.
Hmm, yeah fair enough. So I'd need to get cleared by my doctor first, then come talk to someone at the gym?

Yeah, exactly. Once your doctor says it's okay, we can have a trainer sit down with you to plan some safe movements. 

Would you like me to have someone from the gym call you next week to check how you're tracking?
Yeah, ok. A call next week sounds alright.

Great, I'll have one of the team give you a shout next week to see how you're getting on. 

Thanks for chatting, Aisha, and I hope that shoulder starts feeling better soon. Have a good one.
